groups.title: Capsule (228902ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (62.5 mg as iron) at a time, 2 times a day, between meals.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which abnormal iron metabolism causes iron to be deposited in the liver and pancreas), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, impaired iron utilisation, iron overload, anaemia due to bone marrow failure, haemolytic anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis or liver cirrhosis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired cardiac or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment or low blood protein.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI and the like), anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene, diphosphonates, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, vitamin E preparations, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If hives, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma, occasional rises in AST and ALT, rare rises in ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, discoloration of the teeth or stomach discomfort appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral suspension (118101ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the antacid action and the improvement of symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet (1.212 g) at a time by mouth, 3 times a day, between meals. The dose is increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are receiving dialysis or have phosphate deficiency.

Do not take this medicine together with tetracycline antibiotics. Because of the adsorbing action of this medicine, or the rise in pH in the digestive tract and body fluids, it may affect the absorption and excretion of medicines taken with it.

Rarely, constipation may occur.

groups.title: Oral suspension (285400ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid (including acid related to gastritis and gastric or duodenal ulcer), heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, an upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and acid belching.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, between meals (between one meal and the next) and at bedtime. Leave at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not give this medicine to a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, or if you have kidney impairment.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine together with tetracycline antibiotics.

If constipation or diarrhoea appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (D82400ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, swelling, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously over a long period. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive (cough suppressant), an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are being given medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, impaired liver function (general lassitude, jaundice), interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine output, swelling of the face and limbs, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache and the like), myopathy (weakness, cramp of the arms or legs, paralysis) or ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (D21000CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the after-care of healed wound tissue (hypertrophic and keloid scars, acne scars and surgical scars).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 2 years and over: apply to the wound and the surrounding skin several times a day and massage in gently. In adults, for hypertrophic scars the medicine may be applied thickly the evening before and held in place with a bandage, so that it stays on overnight.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 6 months of age; if you have a hypersensitivity reaction to heparin, a tendency to bleed or a low platelet count; on incised or unhealed wounds, on mucous membranes and/or on areas with purulent infection; or if you are pregnant.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are breast-feeding or if the user is a baby under 2 years of age.

Do not apply it around the eyes or to mucous membranes. Take care that the scar is not exposed to strong sunlight or to light. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. For children, and especially for babies, it is not appropriate to hold the medicine in place with a bandage overnight.

While using this medicine, do not use it together with anticoagulants (coumarin, aspirin, dipyridamole, dextran, streptokinase).

If an allergic reaction appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (123201CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for whitening the teeth.
groups.usage: First check that the mouth is healthy, then brush the teeth thoroughly and keep the mouth clean. Make an impression of the teeth to produce a model, and on the model apply block-out resin 0.5 mm thick over the front of the teeth that are to be whitened, to create space for the material. Cure the model in a light-curing unit for 30 seconds. Using the cured model and an Omnivac, make the plastic tray that will be fitted on the teeth. Trim the tray with scissors to fit the teeth, cutting from 0.5 mm above the gum line, then fill the tray about 1/2 full with this medicine. Fit the tray on the teeth, brush off any gel that comes out beyond the gums, and brush the teeth. Wear the tray 1 time each day for about 4 hours, for about 10 days.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have an infection or a wound inside the mouth, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if the user is under 18 years of age.

This medicine must not be eaten; if it is swallowed by mistake, make yourself vomit immediately. Where possible, keep it from touching the gums directly; if it does touch them, rinse with water immediately. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, rinse them with water immediately and consult a doctor.

It is advisable to avoid tobacco, coffee and juice during treatment.

Irritation of the gums, the teeth and the digestive tract may occur (in severe cases it may cause inflammation).

groups.title: Cream (341900CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eczema, dermatitis, prickly heat, dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, itching, insect bites and hives.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on infants aged 30 months or under.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms from a medicine or a cosmetic (rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like), if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe wet or eroded (macerated) skin, or if the user is a child.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Use this medicine externally only; it must not be used internally. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, rinse the eyes with water immediately.

If rash, redness, itching or swelling appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (A80000ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent and relieve the dizziness, vomiting and headache caused by motion sickness.
groups.usage: To prevent motion sickness, take one dose 30 minutes before boarding. The single dose by age group is: people aged 15 years and over, 1 bottle (30 mL); ages 11 years to under 15 years, 2/3 bottle (20 mL); ages 7 years to under 11 years, 1/2 bottle (15 mL); ages 3 years to under 7 years, 1/3 bottle (10 mL). If a further dose is needed, take one dose leaving an interval of at least 4 hours, up to a limit of 2 doses in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are breast-feeding, or if the user is a baby or young child under 3 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a heart disorder; if you are debilitated; if the user is an older person; if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other anti-emetics, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, antitussives and expectorants, or gastrointestinal analgesics and antispasmodics. Avoid alcoholic drinks while taking this medicine.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, headache, facial flushing, sensitivity to light, difficulty passing urine, thirst or constipation appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (A36900APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin C, vitamin B2 and vitamin E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, and in old age; to relieve pigmentation (melasma, freckles) caused by sunlight, skin disease and the like; and to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds.
groups.usage: Children aged 24 months to under 8 years: take 1/2 sachet at a time. Children aged 8 years and over and adults: take 1 sachet at a time. Take the dose 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, a premature baby or a young child; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine), gout, kidney stones or a tendency to thrombosis (blocked blood vessels).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine together with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness of the skin, nausea or vomiting appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (C45100ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin E, vitamin B1, vitamin B2 and vitamin B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, and in old age; to relieve the symptoms of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of the menopause such as stiff shoulders and neck, numb hands and feet, cold hands and feet, neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); to relieve angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 8 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soy or peanuts, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, a premature baby or a young child; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or need to be given lipid emulsions with care; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis (blocked blood vessels); if you are short of folic acid; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

Do not take this medicine together with levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen or with intravenous lipid preparations.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), nausea, vomiting, loose stools, inflammation of the mouth, loss of appetite or abdominal bloating appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye drops (228835COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for spring keratitis or conjunctivitis and for allergic conjunctivitis.
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the eye at a time, 4 times a day (morning, midday, evening and before going to bed). The amount is increased or decreased as appropriate according to symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to benzalkonium chloride.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Avoid wearing soft contact lenses while using this medicine. Use this medicine only in the eye. Do not use any liquid that is left 1 month after opening.

Occasionally, temporary eye irritation, a burning feeling, stinging, redness of the conjunctiva, swelling of the conjunctiva or inflammation of the eyelid may occur on instillation, and rarely conjunctivitis or a hypersensitivity reaction may occur.

groups.title: Eye drops (D60200COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for washing the eyes, for eye discomfort after swimming, and when dust or sweat has got into the eyes.
groups.usage: Wash the eye using 5 mL at a time, 3 to 6 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on infants aged 30 months or under.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain; if you have ever had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (for example redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash or reddening of the skin); if you have been diagnosed with dry eye syndrome; if the user is a child; or if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine only for washing the eyes. Do not use it as a wetting solution for contact lenses or while contact lenses are being worn. To prevent contamination, do not share the eye cup with others. Do not use it on an injured eye. If there is no improvement in symptoms after several days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or skin rash, redness or itching appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (B10100ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle (30 mL) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is an older person or is debilitated; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a high fever; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or ulcer or bleeding problems; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take this medicine continuously over a long period. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Granules (C21300AGN)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occur in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, swelling, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot absorb fluid; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with diuretics, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide). Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding in the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, hearing loss, swelling, ringing in the ears, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), asthma, impaired liver function (general lassitude, jaundice and the like), interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine output, swelling of the face and limbs, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache and the like) or myopathy (weakness, cramp of the arms or legs, paralysis) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (110702ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve headache, toothache, sore throat, period pain, muscle and joint pain, low back pain and mild arthritis pain, and to relieve the pain and fever caused by a cold.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 2 tablets (500 to 1000 mg) at a time, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of 8 tablets (4000 mg).
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause bleeding in the digestive tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to salicylate preparations, peptic ulcer, aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and the like) or a history of it, haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or a tendency to bleed; if you are also being given methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more per week (15 mg/week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or abnormal cardiovascular circulation (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis, a major bleeding event and the like); if you have liver impairment or abnormal heart function; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is an older person; if you have severe glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; or if the user is under 15 years of age with chickenpox or influenza.

Do not use this medicine together with methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more per week (15 mg/week), with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or with salicylate preparations. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking anticoagulants, thrombolytics or other platelet aggregation inhibitors, haemostatics, diabetes medicines (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), uricosuric medicines (benzbromarone, probenecid), low-dose methotrexate, acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin), lithium preparations, ibuprofen, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemic corticosteroid preparations (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or valproic acid.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, hives and the like), redness of the skin, itching, a blocked nose, cardiac or respiratory disturbance, or — occasionally — rash, swelling, hives, rhinitis-like symptoms or conjunctivitis appear, or — rarely — Lyell's syndrome (toxic epidermal necrolysis), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) presenting as fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, facial swelling, hepatitis, nephritis, blood abnormalities, myocarditis or myositis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anaemia, anaemia, low white blood cell count, low platelet count, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, bleeding in the digestive tract, peptic ulcer and perforation, ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, liver impairment, kidney impairment, acute kidney failure, hyperventilation, symptoms of metabolic acidosis or Conn's syndrome appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (163601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for venous and lymphatic insufficiency (swelling of the legs, pain, early pressure sores) and for haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: For venous disease: take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day, with breakfast and with dinner. For acute haemorrhoids: for the first 4 days take 3 tablets at a time, 2 times a day; for the next 3 days take 2 tablets at a time, 2 times a day, in the morning and in the evening.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to them, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are breast-feeding. Do not breast-feed while taking this medicine.

If diarrhoea, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, or — rarely — light-headedness, headache, lassitude, rash, itching or hives, or — occasionally — colitis, or abdominal pain of unknown frequency, swelling of the face, lips or eyelids, or exceptionally Quincke's oedema appears, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (225402APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to regulate the bowel and to improve constipation, loose stools, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen and abnormal fermentation in the intestine when the intestinal flora is disturbed (for example by antibiotics or chemotherapy).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 to 2 sachets at a time, 2 times a day. Children aged 3 to 12 years: take 1 sachet at a time, 3 times a day. Children under 3 years of age: take 1 sachet at a time, 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a central venous catheter in place, if you are critically ill or immunodeficient, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

If itching, hives, skin rash, angioedema, an anaphylactic reaction, wind, constipation or fungaemia appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated tablet (D48400ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and to relieve the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that go with constipation.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 3 tablets at a time. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time. Take the dose once a day at bedtime. For the first dose, however, take the smallest amount, then increase or reduce it a little at a time while watching the form and condition of the stools.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or if the user is a child aged 7 years or under.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain or nausea and vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure; if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5; or if the user is a child aged 10 years or under.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablet. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after an antacid or milk. If you are taking other medicines, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
